source.citation: Merrill, William L. et al. 2020. El Diccionario Tarahumara–Alemán de Matthäus Steffel: Lengua y Cultura Rarámuri en el Siglo XVIII. Universidad de Sonora.
source.type: modern linguistic analysis of Steffel's historical corpus

findings.analysis: -ameke on a verbal base is adjectivizer/nominalizer [participial]
Merrill states that -ameke is one of the suffix chains containing two or more suffixes and identifies final -kV as a reduplicative suffix visible in -ameke, -leke, -liki and -rúgameke.
findings.distribution_note: Approximately three hundred Steffel words end in [k] plus a vowel duplicating the preceding vowel; Merrill calls this the reduplicative suffix -kV.

findings.analysis: In mátschirujégameke, Merrill excludes optional -ke and analyzes the remaining word as base matschí + causative -ruje + stative -ga/-ja + participial -(a)me.
Merrill analyzes -rúgameke as four morphemes: -ru + -ga + -me + -ke; -(a)me is participial and -ke is optional reduplicative.

interpretation.historical_source_level: Steffel himself explicitly identifies ameke as participial and reports frequent omission of final ke, but does not formulate a modern morpheme-by-morpheme segmentation ame + ke.
interpretation.modern_analysis_level: Merrill independently supplies that segmentation for Steffel's corpus: participial -(a)me plus optional reduplicative -kV/-ke in relevant suffix chains.
interpretation.diachronic_effect: This substantially strengthens comparison with modern participial -ame because the historical corpus has an independently analyzed participial morpheme -(a)me rather than only an unanalyzed ending ameke.
interpretation.remaining_limit: The analysis does not by itself establish that every historical surface -ameke has identical internal structure in every lexical class, nor does it prove direct continuity into every modern -ami form.
